svg.text: The full detection pipeline: from webcam frame to consensus-driven arm actuation
The webcam opens once via DirectShow and captures a live frame every second.
Each frame is saved as temp.jpg in the working directory — shared with
MonitorAppweb for the live dashboard snapshot.
Compares current frame against last "no animal" baseline using pixel-level RGB delta.
Only when pixels change beyond ~10% threshold does it proceed to inference.
Frame is resized, base64-encoded, and sent to a local Ollama instance for animal classification.
A single "bad animal" detection does NOT close the gate.
Requires 3 consecutive bad-animal votes (~3 seconds) before action.
Good-vote resets the counter — no false closures.
Energize motor → drive to closed position → wait 15s → de-energize. Persists state to state.txt.
Gate stays closed even after the animal leaves. Reopens only when BOTH conditions are met:
Protects legitimate cat visitors from being spooked by false positives,
while maintaining a firm hold on the gate long enough for any bad animal to move away.
Open how-it-works.html locally for a clickable demo of the consensus buffer
